    CV

    Jorge Luis Briseño-Gómez

    Theoretical & computational physicist — electron–matter interactions

    jorgeluisbrisenio@ciencias.unam.mx
    https://luisbrise.github.io/
    Mexico City, , MX
    Google Scholar ORCID GitHub LinkedIn

    Summary

    Theoretical and computational physicist developing semianalytical electrodynamic models and high-performance numerical codes (C++/Fortran/Python) for electron–nanostructure interactions. Built a linear and angular momentum transfer framework for swift electrons interacting with nanoparticles that reduces single-configuration runtimes from hours to seconds, and used it to show that the sign of the transferred momentum is robust across every material, size, and geometry combination tested. Extended this expertise to quantitative STEM-EELS theory during an international research stay at Uppsala University (Sweden), reformulating magnetic multislice simulations in Fourier space to remove prior real-space cutoffs and cut magnon-spectroscopy propagation times from hours to seconds-to-minutes.

    Work Experience

    • PhD Guest Researcher
      2025-09-08 - 2026-03-08
      Materials Theory Division, Department of Physics and Astronomy, Uppsala University
      Magnetic Multislice Calculations
      • Reduced multislice propagation time for magnetic-scattering EELS simulations from hours to seconds–minutes (depending on cell size) by incorporating the FDES algorithm into the existing mult_proj.f90 implementation.
      • Eliminated the real-space cutoff for the (formally infinite-range) magnetic vector potential by evaluating the highly oscillatory kernel integrals via FFTLog and computing the potential exactly in Fourier space.
      • Applying the resulting Magnetic Multislice code, together with TACAW methods, to predict the EELS spectrum of magnons.
    • PhD Researcher
      2023 - 2027
      Graduate Program in Physical Sciences (UNAM)
      Linear and Angular Momentum Transfer from Swift Electrons to Nanoparticles; Side project: Causal, Non-local Dielectric Response (led by D. Espinosa-González); Side project: Time-Resolved Recoil Force on Nanoparticles (led by E. E. Viveros-Armas)
      • Developed an efficient numerical framework for linear and angular momentum transfer from swift electrons to large nanoparticles, reducing the runtime for a single particle configuration from hours to seconds.
      • Showed that the sign of the transferred momentum does not reverse for any material, size, or geometry combination tested.
      • Presenting findings at international conferences (M&M, FiO) and preparing manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication.
      • Contributing the underlying momentum-transfer framework and theoretical support to an extension with a fully causal, non-local dielectric response.
      • Contributing the underlying framework and theoretical support to an extension resolving the time-dependent recoil force on the nanoparticle.
    • Master’s Research Fellow
      2021 - 2023
      Graduate Program in Physical Sciences (UNAM)
      Angular Momentum Transfer from Swift Electrons to Nanoparticles
      • Derived the dipole-approximation framework for angular momentum transfer from swift electrons to nanoparticles.
      • Culminating dissertation with Honorable Mention (Mención Honorífica).
      • Explored the impact of nanoparticle geometry and size on momentum transfer.
      • Presented research at international conferences and departmental seminars.
    • Assistant Researcher
      2017 - 2021
      School of Science, UNAM
      Induced EMF on the Moon; Absorption and scattering of light by small particles
      • Developed numerical codes for electromagnetic induction using lunar motion.
      • Prepared manuscripts; produced BSc thesis.
      • Exact solutions + numerical simulations; figures/manuscripts.
    • Assistant Researcher
      2017 - 2017
      National Institute of Nuclear Research (ININ)
      Plasma profiles within a Tokamak nuclear fusion reactor
      • Supported numerical simulations; technical reports.
